title: IoT Air Quality Monitoring System with Real-Time Web Dashboard
description: Full-stack IoT application that collects TVOC and eCO₂ measurements from an M5Stack device, stores them in a database, and displays the data through a responsive web dashboard with live updates, historical records, and environmental statistics.
details:
Designed and implemented a complete IoT monitoring system for measuring indoor air quality using an M5Stack device equipped with a TVOC/eCO₂ gas sensor. 

The embedded device was programmed in UIFlow to collect air quality measurements once per minute, display the latest readings on the device's screen, and transmit the data as JSON via HTTP POST requests to a cloud-hosted server. A Remote+ interface was also implemented, allowing users to monitor the latest sensor values and remotely control the device's display backlight from a smartphone. 

On the backend, a Python Flask application hosted on PythonAnywhere receives incoming measurements, validates the data, timestamps each reading, and stores it in an SQLite database. The server exposes web pages and API endpoints that provide both current and historical measurement data. 

 The frontend consists of two dynamic web pages built with HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. The dashboard displays the most recent measurements together with minimum and maximum recorded values, while a dedicated history page presents all stored measurements using pagination for improved usability. To avoid full-page reloads, the application uses AJAX (XMLHttpRequest) to periodically fetch updated data from the server, providing near real-time monitoring. 

 Throughout the project, emphasis was placed on data validation, client-server communication, RESTful API design, database management, asynchronous JavaScript, and cloud deployment.
